transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood Product), Sophie Kim (NovaEdge PM), Liam O'Connor (NovaEdge Eng), Ravi Menon (NovaEdge SA)

Summary: (auto) Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing workflow, reference architecture for private deployments, and plan a joint performance benchmark. Action items captured below.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. uh we'll run through listing checklist, reference arch, benchmarks. Sophie, you wanna kick off with any updates from NovaEdge side?
[00:06] Sophie Kim: Yeah thanks Alex, um quick context, marketplace team pushed a deadline for mid June for new integrations. so we need to make sure all assets, images, metadata are ready, and also that the reference arch docs are in a format the marketplace requires. also we've got a staging environment for validation but it's not fully mature yet.
[00:22] Alex Chen: Got it. and when you say staging not mature, is that around manifest validation or auth?
[00:27] Sophie Kim: it's a bit of both. Liam is on the eng side so i'll let him explain.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: yeah the staging endpoint is up but the schema validation is stricter than prod; some of the fields we normally omit are required there. for example we need a service_catalog entry for private deployments, and the asset bundle needs an enhanced README. so we'll need Redwood to provide those artifacts.
[00:45] Priya Patel: ok sounds straightforward. from a Redwood side we'll need to confirm the reference arch shows both Hosted, Dedicated and Private flow, and call out network patterns: VPC peering, transit gateway, and KMS/HSM for keys. do you have a preferred template for network diagrams?
[01:02] Sophie Kim: we prefer SVG + a markdown doc, the marketplace renderer uses the markdown. also any architecture diagrams should have layered views: control plane vs data plane.
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: good note - we'll include both. Priya, i'd propose we do a short diagram for the marketplace listing (high-level) and a separate detailed ref-arch PDF for the partner docs.
[01:23] Ravi Menon: one question on the private deployment flow - how does Redwood handle audit logs and key management in Private? we need to present this in the listing.
[01:31] Priya Patel: yes so for Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations and we can integrate with HSMs; audit logs are exported to customer S3 or SIEM via our console, with retention policies configurable. i'll add exact config snippets in the ref-arch doc.
[01:50] Sophie Kim: perfect, that's exactly what the marketplace security checklist wants - mention of KMS, SOC2, encryption at rest and in transit.
[01:58] Alex Chen: on SOC2/ISO, we can add a link to our compliance pack. i'll attach that in the assets.
[02:05] Liam O'Connor: another area: packaging and runtime compatibility. marketplace requires specific container image labels and a compatibility matrix for supported GPUs and quantization profiles. do you have a canonical list?
[02:17] Priya Patel: we do - we'll share the model compatibility matrix and quantization recommendation doc. note that some of our recommendations differ by compute target (A100 vs H100 vs T4) and by dedicated vs private deployment.
[02:29] Sophie Kim: great. on the listing side, we also need a quick demo video (60-90s) and 3 screenshots of the integration UI. can Redwood produce that?
[02:38] Alex Chen: yes we can. we'll produce a short demo vid and the screenshots. Marco, can you own the video assets?
[02:43] Marco Ruiz: yep can do, i'll coordinate with product marketing.
[02:47] (short crosstalk)
[02:50] Sophie Kim: timeline wise if you can have assets by the 5th we can validate in staging and push to the marketplace by the 15th.
[02:58] Alex Chen: ok that's tight but doable. next up - reference arch specifics. Priya?
[03:03] Priya Patel: i'll walk through the high level then open to Qs. first, we show three deployment profiles: Hosted API (our standard), Dedicated reserved capacity with isolated GPU pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). for the marketplace doc we should highlight when a customer would choose each, and include SLOs and expected throughput numbers.
[03:21] Priya Patel: for Private we'll include network diagrams: options for VPC peering, transit gateways, and a direct connect / express route option. also KMS integration patterns, and where KV cache / prefix caching is stored - note that in Private mode the KV cache exists on customer-managed infra and our runtime can be configured to respect data residency.
[03:40] Ravi Menon: can you clarify what gets sent back to Redwood in Private? some customers are worried about telemetry and keys.
[03:47] Priya Patel: short answer: minimal telemetry. we collect service health metrics only and all payloads can be configured to not leave customer network; audit logs and usage can be pushed to the customer's S3. keys are never stored in plaintext on our side; KMS calls can be proxied by the customer. we'll document the exact flags.
[04:03] Sophie Kim: good. also marketplace reviewers often ask about fallback behavior - if Dedicated capacity is saturated, does Redwood auto-failover to hosted and are data egress concerns addressed?
[04:13] Alex Chen: yes we support smart routing and fallback policies, but for marketplace listing we need to be explicit. fallback to Hosted only happens if customer opt-in; for Private we respect strict isolation and won't route to hosted. we'll add a small decision table to the ref-arch.
[04:30] Liam O'Connor: on benchmarking - we need some numbers for latency: p50/p90/p99 under typical customer load. can Redwood run a short benchmark for our Marketplace validation?
[04:39] Priya Patel: absolutely. we can run Dedicated vs Hosted comparisons. propose a joint run: NovaEdge provides representative prompt set + sequence length distribution, we run tests on our Dedicated config (x cards) and return metrics.
[04:52] Sophie Kim: timeline?
[04:53] Priya Patel: if you provide datasets by 2026-06-09 we can run experiments week of 6/15 and present results 6/18.
[05:00] Sophie Kim: sounds good. i'll confirm.
[05:03] (pause)
[05:07] Alex Chen: quick question re: marketplace manifest - do you require signed artifacts?
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: we prefer checksums and signature metadata in the manifest. not a hard crypto signature for partners but it's moving that direction.
[05:20] Marco Ruiz: we'll include checksums and versioned artifacts.
[05:23] Sophie Kim: also on pricing/plan mapping - marketplace needs clear entitlements. from Redwood side, can you provide SKU mappings for Dedicated reserved tiers vs Hosted usage?
[05:34] Alex Chen: yes we'll provide SKU mapping + recommended default pricing tiers for the listing. legal/finance will follow up for exact contract language but we can provide the mapping.
[05:42] Sophie Kim: excellent. another security question: SSO and provisioning - marketplace typically wants SAML metadata for the integration. can Redwood supply SAML metadata and example SSO flow?
[05:52] Priya Patel: yes, we support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and can provide SAML metadata and an example provisioning flow; note that for Private deployments customers often handle SSO externally so we'll document both options.
[06:05] Ravi Menon: one more technical - quantization and model variants: the marketplace requires we declare which variants are supported in dedicated vs private; do you have a clear matrix?
[06:14] Priya Patel: yes, we'll share the matrix. short note: 8-bit quantized models supported on Dedicated x86 setups; 4-bit on certain H100 configs with tradeoffs. we'll annotate recommended defaults.
[06:27] Sophie Kim: awesome. last bit: do you have any legal/marketing blurbs we should use? short description, long description, feature bullets?
[06:36] Alex Chen: yes we'll provide short/long descriptions and 3-5 feature bullets. we'll also give a short 60s demo script for Marco to produce the video.
[06:45] Sophie Kim: perfect. i think that covers the main items. any open risks?
[06:50] Alex Chen: primary risk is staging validation flakiness, and timeline. we'll mitigate with an early asset drop by 6/5 and a quick smoke test.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: yep i'll do a smoke validation once assets land.
[07:02] Marco Ruiz: i'll queue the video work and PM will review.
[07:06] Priya Patel: ok i'll start the ref-arch draft and include configuration snippets for KMS/SAML/egress controls.
[07:13] Sophie Kim: great. can we recap actions?
[07:16] Alex Chen: sure - Alex sends checklist by 6/5; Priya draft ref-arch by 6/10; Sophie provide staging account + deadlines by 6/8; Liam provide manifest sample by 6/12; joint benchmark dataset by 6/9; schedule benchmark week of 6/15.
[07:33] Sophie Kim: yep that's correct, thanks everyone.
[07:36] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and share links: marketplace checklist (link: https://redwood.example.com/marketplace-checklist), ref-arch template (link: https://redwood.example.com/ref-arch-template).
[07:50] (meeting ends)
